relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period increases with the square root of its length and decreases as gravity strengthens, while bob mass has no effect. Larger release angles slightly lengthen the period beyond the small-angle rule.
assumptions: The string is massless and inelastic, with all mass concentrated at the bob.
Pivot friction and air resistance are neglected.
Large release angles add a small correction to the small-angle period.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the pendulum bob, which does not change the swing period.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical that controls the swing amplitude.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration acting on the bob.

quantities.label: Swing period
quantities.meaning: Actual time for one full back-and-forth cycle including angle effects.

quantities.label: Small-angle period
quantities.meaning: Ideal period predicted by 2 pi sqrt(L / g) for small swings.

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle of the pendulum from vertical at time t.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the bob at the lowest point of its swing.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.length; var g = 9.81; var angle0 = 60; var theta0 = angle0 * Math.PI / 180; var k = Math.sin(0.5 * theta0); var a = 1; var b = Math.sqrt(1 - k * k); for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++) { var an = 0.5 * (a + b); var bn = Math.sqrt(a * b); a = an; b = bn; } var kFactor = 1 / a; var smallAnglePeriod = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var period = smallAnglePeriod * kFactor; var omega = 2 * Math.PI / period; var omega0 = 2 * Math.PI / smallAnglePeriod; var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var thetaIdeal = theta0 * Math.cos(omega0 * t); var angle = theta * 180 / Math.PI; var idealAngle = thetaIdeal * 180 / Math.PI; var maxSpeed = 2 * Math.sqrt(g * L) * k; var bobX = L * Math.sin(theta); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(theta); var speedMag = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 2 * g * L * (Math.cos(theta) - Math.cos(theta0)))); var dirSign = Math.sin(omega * t) >= 0 ? -1 : 1; var speed = dirSign * speedMag; var vx = speed * Math.cos(theta); var vy = speed * Math.sin(theta); var arrowScale = 0.15; var velTipX = bobX + arrowScale * vx; var velTipY = bobY + arrowScale * vy; var idealX = L * Math.sin(thetaIdeal); var idealY = -L * Math.cos(thetaIdeal); var releaseX = L * Math.sin(theta0); var releaseY = -L * Math.cos(theta0); var refBottomY = -L - 0.15; return { period: period, small_angle_period: smallAnglePeriod, angle: angle, ideal_angle: idealAngle, max_speed: maxSpeed, bob_x: bobX, bob_y: bobY, vel_tip_x: velTipX, vel_tip_y: velTipY, ideal_x: idealX, ideal_y: idealY, release_x: releaseX, release_y: releaseY, ref_bottom_y: refBottomY, is_short: L < 0.85, is_long: L > 1.35 }; }

Long string: slow swings, higher v

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum's Swing?
lesson.description: Watch a pendulum swing from a 60 degree angle alongside a small-angle reference marker. Slide the string length to see how period and speed respond.
lesson.instructions: Drag the String length slider between 0.5 m and 2.0 m while watching the swing, the velocity arrow, and the Swing Angle vs Time plot. Compare the pendulum bob with the small-angle dot to spot the extra delay from a 60 degree release.
lesson.goal: A pendulum's period grows with the square root of string length, quadrupling length doubles the period, and large angles add a slight delay.
